1.heading: The Logos, creation, light, witness, and incarnation
1.note: All things were made through him; John is sent to testify about the light; the Word 'became flesh and lived among us'

1.heading: John denies rival titles and identifies Jesus
1.note: Priests ask John who he is; he says he is not the Christ, then points to Jesus as 'the Lamb of God'

1.heading: Testimony and ‘come and see’ gather the first disciples
1.note: Two of John's disciples follow Jesus; Andrew brings Simon, Jesus says 'Follow me' to Philip, and Jesus says he saw Nathanael under the fig tree

2.heading: Cana's need becomes the first sign of glory
2.note: Jesus's mother says they have no wine; servants fill six stone water pots, and the ruler of the feast tastes water now become wine

2.heading: Jesus goes to Jerusalem and clears the temple courts
2.note: Jesus stays in Capernaum, then goes up to Jerusalem, drives out sheep and oxen with a whip of cords, and overthrows tables

2.heading: The temple riddle and fragile sign-based belief
2.note: Asked for a sign, Jesus says 'I will raise it up' in three days; many believe, but he does not entrust himself to them

3.heading: Nicodemus hears earthly repetition where Jesus speaks of birth from above
3.note: Nicodemus comes by night; Jesus says one must be 'born anew', and Nicodemus asks if a man can enter his mother's womb again

3.heading: The lifted-up Son reveals God's saving love and the crisis of light
3.note: As Moses lifted up the serpent, so the Son of Man must be lifted up; God gave his Son, and men loved the darkness

3.heading: John the Baptist refuses rivalry and rejoices in the bridegroom
3.note: John's disciples report that Jesus baptizes and everyone is coming to him; John answers 'He must increase, but I must decrease'

4.heading: At Jacob's well, thirst opens a conversation about living water and worship
4.note: Tired, Jesus asks a Samaritan woman at Jacob's well for a drink, offers living water, and says she has had five husbands

4.heading: The woman witnesses while disciples misunderstand food and harvest
4.note: Leaving her water pot, the woman tells the people 'Come, see a man'; disciples urge Jesus to eat, and many Samaritans believe

4.heading: A royal official believes Jesus's word and his household sees life restored
4.note: In Cana a nobleman begs Jesus to heal his dying son; Jesus says 'Your son lives', and servants say the fever left him

5.heading: Jesus heals a long-disabled man at the pool
5.note: A man sick thirty-eight years says no one puts him into the pool; Jesus says 'take up your mat, and walk' and he does

5.heading: The Sabbath command provokes conflict and further encounter
5.note: The Jews say carrying the mat is not lawful; Jesus finds the man in the temple, and the Jews seek to kill Jesus

5.heading: The Son gives life, judges, and acts in unity with the Father
5.note: The Son does what he sees the Father doing and gives life to whom he desires; all in the tombs will hear his voice

5.heading: John, the works, the Father, and Scripture testify
5.note: Jesus names his witnesses: John, his works, the Father, and the Scriptures; he adds that Moses accuses them

6.heading: Jesus feeds five thousand and refuses imposed kingship
6.note: Jesus gives thanks over five barley loaves and two fish, the disciples distribute them to about five thousand men, and twelve baskets are left

6.heading: Jesus crosses the sea and identifies himself to the disciples
6.note: In the dark, with a great wind blowing, the disciples see Jesus walking on the sea and are afraid; he says 'It is I'

6.heading: The crowd seeks bread while Jesus speaks of the Father's true bread
6.note: The crowd crosses by boat seeking Jesus; he says they ate the loaves and were filled, and declares 'I am the bread of life'

6.heading: Flesh, blood, and descent from heaven intensify the dispute
6.note: The Jews murmur that he came down out of heaven; Jesus says the bread he gives is his flesh, and they must eat it

6.heading: Many leave; Peter confesses; Judas is foreshadowed
6.note: Many disciples call it a hard saying and go back; Peter says 'You have the words of eternal life', and Jesus speaks of Judas

7.heading: Jesus rejects his brothers' timetable and goes to the feast privately
7.note: His brothers tell him to go into Judea and reveal himself; Jesus says his time has not yet come, then goes up in secret

7.heading: Temple teaching divides the crowd over authority, Sabbath, and origin
7.note: Midway through the feast Jesus teaches in the temple; the Jews marvel, they seek to take him, and officers are sent to arrest him

7.heading: Jesus promises living water and the Spirit at the feast's climax
7.note: Jesus stands and cries out for the thirsty to come and drink; 'rivers of living water' will flow from within the believer

7.heading: Prophetic and legal disputes divide crowd, guards, and leaders
7.note: Some say prophet, others Christ; the officers say 'No man ever spoke like this man'; Nicodemus asks about the law, and everyone goes home

8.heading: Jesus refuses a trap built around an accused woman
8.note: Scribes and Pharisees bring a woman taken in adultery; Jesus says 'let him throw the first stone', and they go out one by one

8.heading: The light of the world debates testimony and origin
8.note: 'I am the light of the world'; the Pharisees say his testimony is not valid, and many believe as he speaks

8.heading: Remaining in Jesus's word leads to truth and freedom
8.note: Jesus tells believing Jews 'the truth will make you free'; they claim Abraham, and he says they are 'of your father the devil'

8.heading: The dispute reaches Abraham, glory, and ‘I AM’
8.note: They call him a Samaritan with a demon; Jesus says 'before Abraham came into existence, I AM', and they take up stones

9.heading: Jesus rejects blame and gives sight through clay and washing
9.note: Asked who sinned, Jesus says neither did; he anoints the blind man's eyes with mud, and the man washes and comes back seeing

9.heading: Pharisees investigate the Sabbath healing and divide
9.note: The man tells the Pharisees he washed and sees; they disagree about Jesus, and his parents say 'He is of age'

9.heading: The healed man answers pressure and is cast out
9.note: They call Jesus a sinner; the man says 'though I was blind, now I see', and when he argues they throw him out

9.heading: Jesus finds him, receives his confession, and names blindness
9.note: Jesus finds the man, who says 'Lord, I believe' and worships him; Pharisees ask if they are blind too, and their sin remains

10.heading: The shepherd enters, calls, and leads while strangers scatter
10.note: Entering by the door, the shepherd calls his sheep by name and goes before them; they follow, but flee from a stranger

10.heading: Jesus is the gate and good shepherd who gives his life
10.note: Jesus says 'I am the door' and 'I am the good shepherd'; the hired hand flees, but the shepherd lays down his life

10.heading: At Dedication Jesus speaks of his sheep and unity with the Father
10.note: In Solomon's porch the Jews ask for a plain answer; he says his sheep hear his voice and 'I and the Father are one'

10.heading: Psalm 82 and the works answer a blasphemy charge
10.note: The Jews take up stones and charge him with blasphemy; he asks which good work, cites 'you are gods', then goes beyond the Jordan

11.heading: News, love, delay, and the dangerous return to Judea
11.note: The sisters send word that Lazarus is sick; Jesus stays two days, then tells the disciples plainly 'Lazarus is dead'

11.heading: Martha meets the resurrection and the life
11.note: Martha meets Jesus, who says 'I am the resurrection and the life'; she answers that she believes he is the Christ

11.heading: Mary, mourners, and Jesus approach the tomb in grief
11.note: Martha calls Mary secretly; Mary falls at Jesus's feet, and troubled Jesus asks 'Where have you laid him'; then 'Jesus wept'

11.heading: Jesus calls Lazarus from the tomb
11.note: Jesus has the stone taken away from the cave, thanks the Father, and cries 'Lazarus, come out'; the dead man comes out bound

11.heading: Belief and fear lead the council to plan Jesus's death
11.note: The council fears the Romans will take away their place and nation; Caiaphas says one man should die for the people

12.heading: Mary anoints Jesus while Judas objects
12.note: Mary anoints Jesus's feet with a pound of nard and wipes them with her hair; Judas asks why it was not sold

12.heading: Jesus enters Jerusalem and Lazarus's sign draws a crowd
12.note: A crowd comes to see Lazarus, and the chief priests plan to kill him; Jesus sits on a young donkey as people cry 'Hosanna'

12.heading: Greeks arrive and Jesus declares the hour of death and glory
12.note: Greeks ask Philip to see Jesus; he says a grain of wheat must die to bear fruit, and a voice speaks from the sky

12.heading: Isaiah frames unbelief and hidden belief
12.note: Despite many signs they do not believe, as Isaiah said; many rulers believe but, because of the Pharisees, do not confess it

12.heading: Jesus summarizes light, judgment, and the Father's command
12.note: Jesus cries out that he came as a light, not to judge but to save the world, and speaks as the Father commanded

13.heading: Jesus washes the disciples' feet and answers Peter
13.note: During supper Jesus wraps a towel around himself and begins to wash the disciples' feet; Peter says 'You will never wash my feet'

13.heading: Lord and Teacher gives a pattern of servant action
13.note: Back at the table Jesus says they call him Teacher and Lord, and so they ought to wash one another's feet

13.heading: Jesus identifies the betrayer, who departs into night
13.note: Troubled, Jesus says one of them will betray him; he gives a dipped piece of bread to Judas, who goes out immediately

13.heading: Glory, the new command, and Peter's denial
13.note: Jesus gives a new commandment to love one another; Peter says he will lay down his life, but is told of three denials

14.heading: Trust, the Father's dwelling, and the way
14.note: Jesus says he goes to prepare a place in his Father's house, and tells Thomas 'I am the way'

14.heading: Seeing Jesus, knowing the Father, and greater works
14.note: Philip asks to be shown the Father; Jesus says he who 'has seen me has seen the Father' and speaks of greater works

14.heading: Another Advocate and mutual indwelling
14.note: Those who love him keep his commandments; the Father will give another Counselor, and Jesus says he will not leave them orphans

14.heading: Spirit-taught memory, Jesus's peace, and departure
14.note: The Holy Spirit will teach all things and remind them of all that Jesus said; he gives his peace, then says to arise

15.heading: The true vine, pruning, remaining, and fruit
15.note: The Father the farmer takes away fruitless branches and prunes fruitful ones; Jesus says 'apart from me you can do nothing'

15.heading: Remain in love through command, joy, and self-giving friendship
15.note: They remain in his love by keeping his commandments; Jesus calls them friends, not servants, and says he chose and appointed them

15.heading: The world's hatred follows its hatred of Jesus
15.note: Jesus says the world hated him before it hated them; they are not of the world, and whoever hates him hates his Father

15.heading: The Advocate and the disciples will testify
15.note: Jesus will send the Counselor, the Spirit of truth, who will testify about him; the disciples will also testify, having been with him

16.heading: Jesus warns of exclusion and mistaken religious violence
16.note: Jesus says they will be put out of the synagogues, and whoever kills them will think he offers service to God

16.heading: Departure permits the Advocate's exposing work
16.note: Jesus says it is to their advantage that he goes away; then the Counselor will convict the world about sin, righteousness, and judgment

16.heading: The Spirit guides and glorifies Jesus
16.note: Jesus has more to say than they can bear now; the Spirit of truth will guide them into all truth and glorify him

16.heading: A little while turns laboring sorrow into joy
16.note: 'A little while' puzzles the disciples; Jesus says they will weep but their sorrow will be turned into joy, like a woman giving birth

16.heading: Plain speech, the Father's love, scattering, and peace
16.note: The disciples say he now speaks plainly; Jesus says they will be scattered and leave him alone, yet 'I have overcome the world'

17.heading: The Son asks for glory and defines eternal life
17.note: Jesus lifts his eyes to heaven and says the time has come; he says eternal life is to know 'the only true God'

17.heading: Jesus prays for disciples given from the world
17.note: Jesus prays for those the Father gave him, not for the world; he says he kept them, and asks the Father to keep them

17.heading: Protection, joy, truth, sanctification, and sending
17.note: Jesus prays they not be taken from the world but kept from the evil one; as the Father sent him, so he sends them

17.heading: Future believers, unity, witness, glory, and love
17.note: Jesus prays for those who will believe through their word that they may all be one, and be with him where he is

18.heading: Jesus is arrested in the garden and protects his disciples
18.note: Judas brings soldiers with torches and weapons; Jesus says 'I am he' and they fall to the ground; Peter cuts off a servant's ear

18.heading: Annas questions Jesus while Peter denies him
18.note: Jesus is led bound to Annas; the high priest asks about his teaching, an officer slaps him, and Peter denies being a disciple

18.heading: Pilate questions Jesus about kingship and truth
18.note: At the Praetorium, Pilate asks Jesus if he is the King of the Jews; Jesus answers 'My Kingdom is not of this world'

18.heading: The crowd chooses Barabbas
18.note: Pilate offers to release the King of the Jews at Passover; they all shout 'Not this man, but Barabbas', a robber

19.heading: Mock kingship and political pressure decide Pilate
19.note: Pilate flogs Jesus, soldiers crown him with thorns, the chief priests shout 'Crucify! Crucify!', and Pilate delivers him to be crucified

19.heading: Jesus is crucified under a trilingual royal title
19.note: At Golgotha Jesus is crucified between two others; Pilate's title reads 'THE KING OF THE JEWS', and soldiers cast lots for his tunic

19.heading: Jesus creates family, completes Scripture, and dies
19.note: Jesus says to his mother 'your son' and to the disciple 'your mother'; then 'It is finished', and he gives up his spirit

19.heading: Pierced body, eyewitness testimony, and fulfillment
19.note: Soldiers break the legs of the other two but find Jesus already dead; one pierces his side and blood and water come out

19.heading: Joseph and Nicodemus bury Jesus in a garden tomb
19.note: Joseph of Arimathaea asks Pilate for the body; Nicodemus brings myrrh and aloes, and they lay Jesus in a new tomb in a garden

20.heading: Mary reports the open tomb; two disciples inspect it
20.note: Mary tells Peter and the other disciple the Lord is taken from the tomb; they run there, and the other disciple 'saw and believed'

20.heading: Jesus calls Mary by name and sends her to the brothers
20.note: Weeping outside the tomb, Mary sees two angels, then Jesus, whom she supposes the gardener; he says 'Mary', and she answers 'Rabboni'

20.heading: Jesus gives peace, commission, Spirit, and authority
20.note: With the doors locked, Jesus stands among the disciples, shows his hands and side, and breathes on them, saying 'Receive the Holy Spirit'

20.heading: Thomas confesses the risen Jesus
20.note: Thomas will not believe unless he sees the nail prints; Jesus tells him 'see my hands', and Thomas answers 'My Lord and my God'

20.heading: The Gospel states why its signs were written
20.note: Jesus did many other signs not written in this book; these are written that you may believe and have life in his name

21.heading: An unproductive night becomes an abundant catch at Jesus's word
21.note: Having caught nothing all night, the disciples cast the net on the right side as Jesus says; Peter throws himself into the sea

21.heading: The risen Jesus hosts breakfast on shore
21.note: They find a fire of coals with fish and bread; Jesus says 'Come and eat breakfast', then gives them the bread and fish

21.heading: Peter's threefold love becomes pastoral commission
21.note: Jesus asks Peter three times if he loves him; Peter says Jesus knows he has affection for him, and is told 'Feed my sheep'

21.heading: Jesus foretells Peter's death and commands following
21.note: Jesus says another will carry Peter where he does not want to go, and tells him 'Follow me'; Peter asks 'what about this man'

21.heading: The beloved disciple's testimony and uncontainable works
21.note: The disciple who testifies wrote these things; the writer supposes the world would not have room for books of everything Jesus did

limits: The sources are old reference works (Thayer's, Strong's, Whiston's Josephus), the Mishnah in Sefaria's English, and Wikipedia. They show a claim is standard; they are not current scholarship.

The reviewers' source quotations came through a page reader that returns short excerpts, and for some long pages a summary. The lead read every proposed edit and outline note but did not re-read the quotations.
Where a guide sentence names an ancient writer the reviewers did not read directly (for example Ovid, Suetonius or Augustine through a reference page), the `basis` says where the statement was read.

The Meta reader's subscription quota ran out partway through this book. A third outside model, `beam-free` through opencode, read the chapters it missed, after the main review; its findings that no claim already covered were checked in a late ledger.
Each reviewer was one pass with a stated bar ("a careful editor would ask: says who?"). A claim below that bar may remain.
Readings marked as readings were not adjudicated.
The drafter of these guides is not recorded; the commit that rewrote them names no model.

Three pastoral lines a reviewer proposed cutting were kept by Garo's ruling, and one proposed softening of the John 1:1 sentence was rejected by the lead; all four are listed as proposed and not applied.
